text: Stock futures turned lower before the open, with Nasdaq 100 futures down roughly 1% to 1.8% in different reports, giving back part of Monday's 6.5% Nasdaq surge.
Nvidia fell about 4% to 5% before the bell after Monday's 31% jump, and QQQ was down about 1.4% in pre-market trading.
Gold's rebound stalled: it slipped to about $3,624 by 6:16 AM ET after touching $3,678 overnight, as traders priced about a 96% chance of a December Fed hike.
Silver fell back toward $42, giving up part of Monday's 4.7% gain, as a firmer dollar and the expiry of December options weighed.
GDX was down about 1.7% to $71.55 in pre-market trading, a bigger drop than gold's.
The 10-year Treasury yield eased about 1 bp to near 4.91% after New York Fed President Williams said inflation is still running too high; a $70 billion 5-year auction is due today.
The dollar index held near 104.4, close to Monday's 20-month high, and USD/JPY stayed near 159, just under the 160 level traders watch for Japanese intervention.
Brent edged down to about $88.97 overnight after Monday's 3.5% fall to a three-month low, and bitcoin slipped to near $60,000 as the tech bounce faded.
